$comment: Life events about your body and mind (D-068).

events.title: The shakes
events.prompt: You notice your hand vibrating gently on the table. That's your fourth espresso today. Or fifth.

outcomes.text: You switch to water. The vibrating stops in an hour. So does your will to live, briefly.
One more. You can hear colours now. You answer three emails in four minutes.

events.title: Something went click
events.prompt: You bend to pick up a pen and your lower back makes a sound like a twig. You are, apparently, old now.

outcomes.text: Ten minutes of careful stretching and it eases. You resolve to do this every day. You won't.
You walk it off. It works, mostly.
You walk it off. It does not walk off. You spend the afternoon at a slight angle.

events.title: Racing thoughts
events.prompt: It's late, the house is quiet, and your brain has chosen now to replay every awkward thing you've said since 2009.

outcomes.text: You write it all down. On paper it's smaller. You put the pen down and breathe.
You scroll until your eyes sting and now you know about a war between two people you've never heard of.
Warm milk, the kitchen light, the hum of the fridge. Nothing is solved, but everything is softer.

events.title: Free check-up in the park
events.prompt: A nurse from Riverdale Health has set up a folding table in the park: "Free blood pressure checks! Takes two minutes!"

outcomes.text: "Textbook," says the nurse. You feel absurdly proud of your arteries.

memory.text: Got a clean bill of health at a park check-up.

outcomes.text: "A little high. Less salt, more sleep, and see your doctor." You nod like you'll do all three.

memory.text: A park check-up said my blood pressure was high.

outcomes.text: You speed up. Ignorance is bliss, or at least it's faster.

events.title: The mirror at the gym
events.prompt: The person on the next machine is lifting twice what you are, and making eye contact with you in the mirror.

outcomes.text: You add weight and do one heroic rep. Your body files a formal complaint, but they nod at you.
You add weight. The weight wins. You pretend you meant to put it down there.
You do your own workout at your own pace. That is, in fact, the whole point.
